message.content: {"summary":"You have covered every required element of the report, with clear structure, STK evidence, hand calculations and a full bibliography. Your introduction and conclusion are specific and well tied to your results. The main gaps are technical: the launch azimuth for your retrograde orbit is described inconsistently, the contact-time and data-budget figures do not reconcile with each other, and the X-band downlink is not supported by a link budget. Correcting these would strengthen an already strong report.","next_steps":["Restate the launch azimuth for your retrograde orbit (i = 97.79°) using a consistent convention, and check β against the sin β = cos i / cos φ relation you cite.","Recalculate the contact fraction (510 s of 771 s is about 66%) and the daily contact time (6 × 510 s is about 51 min), then align Table 6 with these values.","Derive the imaged area and raw data volume from your orbit and access results, and add a link budget for the X-band downlink before claiming all images reach the ground in a day."],"criteria":{"C1":"You clearly state the primary mission, why it is needed, the single-spacecraft configuration and the operator and customers, with literature cited for the bleaching problem. The single-satellite rationale relies mainly on assertion. A brief quantified trade-off against multi-satellite options would make this section more persuasive.","C2":"This is a thorough design, supported by STK figures, access tables, hand calculations and an appendix file list. Your launch, orbit and end-of-life sections are well evidenced. Inaccuracies to fix are the retrograde launch azimuth wording, the 66% versus 60% contact figure, the one-strip-per-day imaging assumption, and the unbudgeted X-band link. Sourcing the Mount Pleasant and Vega C claims would also help.","C3":"Your conclusions are specific and link back to quantified results such as the 5-day revisit, the 3.5 margin and the roughly 2-year decay. You also identify concrete limitations with fallback options. Claims such as the weekly coverage reef managers prefer need a source, and the conclusions would be stronger if they reflected the corrected contact and data figures.","C4":"The report follows a clear engineering structure, with an executive summary, numbered and captioned tables and figures, and in-text citations matching the 15-entry bibliography. Writing is easy to follow. Harmonise the elevation mask: the access report uses 0° while the data budget uses 10°, and a single consistent setting would remove this inconsistency."}}
